newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission rejects British bid to cut BSE cull.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission rejects British bid to cut BSE cull.

text.p: The European Commission rejected on Tuesday a British bid to reduce a cull of cattle most at risk from mad cow disease, a Commission spokesman said.

The spokesman said European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler had expressed concern about possible British plans to limit the cull, noting it was an integral part of an agreement for eventually lifting the bloc's worldwide ban on British beef exports.
"The commissioner was disappointed with the lack of progress in implementing the...agreement," Commission agriculture spokesman Gerard Kiely said.

He was speaking after British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg had reported to EU farm ministers on new scientific findings and on steps by Britain to implement the agreement, which was reached by EU leaders in June.

The British government is considering cutting back an extra cull of an estimated 147,000 animals after a report last month by Oxford University that bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) would die out within five years even without a cull.
Kiely said it was widely recognised that the epidemic would disappear early next century if the eradication measures were implemented.
